review.summary: Single-line fix in countknots: the multiplicity of a knot value t was computed via searchsorted on the AbstractKnotVector wrapper with the default ordering (isless). The fix searches the underlying vector via _vec(k) and passes lt=< explicitly. Because isless and < disagree for floating-point edge cases (notably -0.0 vs 0.0, and NaN), the previous code could return an incorrect multiplicity for such knot values, which propagates into any logic depending on knot multiplicity (e.g. degree/continuity or basis function support). This is a behavioral correctness fix, not a feature, refactor, or diagnostic change.
review.evidence: Minimized production patch is a single hunk touching only the return expression of countknots in src/_KnotVector.jl; minimization reports globally_minimal with all hunks necessary, so the behavior difference is attributable to this one expression. Runtime evidence reports strict_differential = stable_differential over 3 repetitions, with the full suite passing on the fixed version, indicating a reproducible pre-fix failure that the change resolves. The semantic nature of the change (switching the comparison from the default isless ordering to <, plus operating on the raw vector) is consistent with a correctness fix rather than an optimization: the retained comment about the faster path is unchanged.

review.suggested_tests: Assert countknots on a knot vector containing -0.0 returns the correct multiplicity when queried with 0.0 and vice versa, comparing against the reference count(==(t), vec) implementation preserved in the comment. Add a property test over random knot vectors asserting countknots(k, t) == count(==(t), BasicBSpline._vec(k)) for every t in the vector plus values not present. Include a case with repeated interior knots to confirm multiplicity greater than one is still returned, and a case with NaN present to confirm no spurious matches. Optionally assert downstream consumers of countknots (multiplicity-dependent basis support or continuity queries) agree with the reference implementation.
